payload.friendly_name: The walk and closure checks behind ports (#556)
payload.purpose_context: #556 (P1, ADR-0075 slice 7, decision 6): RegistrationImpact, ImpactRelations, FallbackProfileRule and PackMutabilityPolicy refuse on the first fault. The slice declares ClosureWalk, ImpactCheck and MutabilityCheck ports in packs.domain, implements them in packs.application, absorbs #517's PackDependents seam, collects every fault, adds a refusal-code parity test against the open-packs expected codes, and amends ADR-0068.
payload.purpose_tldr: Put the closure walk, impact and mutability checks behind kernel-Rule ports that collect every fault, with a code parity test.

options: (a) problem code = first fault (fixed rule order), violations[] = every fault with its own code, packs = union (additive contract change)
(b) new catch-all code closure_invalid with violations
(c) keep one fault per refusal at the API; collect only internally
payload.question: D1: How does one HTTP refusal carry the collected faults?

options: (a) issue minimum: ImpactRelations 7 rules + FallbackProfileRule 4 checks
(b) (a) + every closure a write joins + role pins, profile enhancement, specialization cycle + every refused write of a registration (mutability) + the qualified-reference checks (ClosureWalk)
payload.question: D2: How far does collect-all reach?

options: (a) absorb: ImpactCheck judges a write and a removal; PackDependents/ClosurePackDependents are deleted; 409 pack_has_dependents stays its own code
(b) keep PackDependents as a sub-port ImpactCheck calls
payload.question: D3: Does ImpactCheck absorb #517 PackDependents?

options: (a) one pass: the port returns Impact(verdict Rationale, notices) and exposes the Rule view; one compose per closure
(b) Rule only; notices from a second compose
payload.question: D4: ImpactCheck is a kernel Rule, but the impact also yields notices (floor/lock/activations). Shape?

options: (a) MutabilityCheck replaces WritePolicyGate outright, collect every refused write
payload.question: D5: MutabilityCheck vs the existing WritePolicyGate port (12 main, 26 test files)?

options: (a) charter-owned mirror packs, each with an open-packs-format expected-code file, plus cases for the collected codes and their order; open-packs charter_service_check.py stays the real gate
(b) read open-packs at its pinned commit in a test
(c) drop: open-packs charter_service_check.py already is the parity test
payload.question: D6: The parity test, given ADR-0070 (charter tests read no open-packs content) and fixtures at tests/fixtures/invalid/?

payload.final_answer: (a) Operator 2026-11-19: the problem code is the first fault's specific code; violations[] lists every fault; packs is the union. Recorded as an additive Changed entry.

(b) Operator 2026-11-19: everything related: every closure a write joins, role pins, profile enhancement, specialization cycle, every refused write of a registration, and the qualified-reference checks.
(a) Operator 2026-11-19: ImpactCheck absorbs PackDependents; PackDependents and ClosurePackDependents are deleted; 409 pack_has_dependents stays its own code.
(a) Operator 2026-11-19: one pass; the port returns the verdict and the notices and exposes the kernel Rule view.
(a) Operator 2026-11-19: MutabilityCheck replaces WritePolicyGate outright and collects every refused write.
(c) Operator 2026-11-19: drop the parity test; open-packs' charter_service_check.py already delivers it. Note this in the spec and on the issue.
